prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses on loans
prov.text:
The Company establishes an allowance as an estimate of the expected credit losses in the loan portfolio at the balance sheet date. Management believes the allowance for credit losses is appropriate based upon management’s best estimate of expected losses within the existing loan portfolio. Should any of the factors considered by management in evaluating the appropriate level of the allowance for credit losses change, the Company’s estimate of expected credit losses could also change which could affect the amount of future provisions for credit losses.

Net loan charge-offs were $4.0 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to net loan charge-offs of $1.7 million for the third quarter of 2025. The rate of net charge-offs to average total loans continues to be at a low level. Net charge-offs of $1.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, were related to purchased credit deteriorated (PCD) loans. At acquisition, the Company identified these loans as credit deteriorated and recorded reserves for expected credit losses. These loans performed in line with expectations subsequent to acquisition.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
Noninterest expense increased by $6.1 million for third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase in noninterest expenses was primarily related to growth in salaries and employee benefits of $4.1 million.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expense increased by $20.1 million compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in noninterest expenses was primarily related to growth in salaries and employee benefits of $13.6 million. The total salaries and employee benefits recorded of $181.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 is after a favorable adjustment to the funded employee benefit trust of $2.8 million. The total salaries and benefits expenses recorded of $167.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 is after a unfavorable adjustment to the funded employee benefit trust of $404,000. Also driving the increase in noninterest expense was net expense from other real estate owned, which increased $2.2 million compared to the same period last year, along with conversion expenses of approximately $1.2 million related to ABOK.

nonop.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonop.text:
Noninterest expense increased by $6.1 million for third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase in noninterest expenses was primarily related to growth in salaries and employee benefits of $4.1 million.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expense increased by $20.1 million compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in noninterest expenses was primarily related to growth in salaries and employee benefits of $13.6 million. The total salaries and employee benefits recorded of $181.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 is after a favorable adjustment to the funded employee benefit trust of $2.8 million. The total salaries and benefits expenses recorded of $167.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 is after a unfavorable adjustment to the funded employee benefit trust of $404,000. Also driving the increase in noninterest expense was net expense from other real estate owned, which increased $2.2 million compared to the same period last year, along with conversion expenses of approximately $1.2 million related to ABOK.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The Company’s effective tax rate was 21.9% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 20.7% for the third quarter of 2025.

The Company’s effective tax rate was 21.6% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 21.2% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

The primary reasons for the difference between the Company’s effective tax rate and the federal statutory rate were tax-exempt income, nondeductible amortization, federal and state tax credits and state tax expense.

net.text: The Company’s net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $67.3 million, compared to $62.7 million for the third quarter of 2025. Diluted net income per common share was $1.97 and $1.85 for the third quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, net interest income, which is the Company’s principal source of operating revenue, increased $10.4 million or 8.3% compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. Higher loan volume and general growth in earning assets were the primary drivers of the change in net interest income. Net interest margin is the ratio of taxable-equivalent net interest income to average earning assets for the period.

Net interest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased $34.3 million or 9.5% compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Higher loan volume and general growth in earning assets were the primary drivers to the increase.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income increased by $1.5 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025. Service charges on deposits and treasury income each increased when compared to third quarter last year.

Noninterest income included non-sufficient funds ("NSF") and overdraft fees totaling $8.9 million and $8.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. This represents 17.4% and 16.6% of the Company’s noninterest income for the respective periods. In addition, the Company had debit card usage and interchange fees totaling $7.2 million and $6.9 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. This represents 14.0% and 13.8% of the Company’s noninterest income for the respective periods.

Noninterest income increased by $9.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Service charges on deposits, securities transactions and treasury income each increased when compared to third quarter last year.

Noninterest income included NSF and overdraft fees totaling $25.0 million and $23.3 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. This represents 16.0% and 15.9% of the Company’s noninterest income for the respective

periods.

intro.text: BancFirst Corporation (the “Company”) is a financial holding company headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma and registered under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the “BHC Act”). It conducts a vast majority of its operating activities through its wholly-owned subsidiary, BancFirst (“BancFirst”), an Oklahoma state-chartered bank headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The Company also conducts operating activities through its wholly-owned subsidiaries, Pegasus Bank (“Pegasus”), a Texas state-chartered bank headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Worthington Bank ("Worthington"), a Texas state-chartered bank headquartered in Arlington, Texas and, prior to its merger with BancFirst in February 2026, American Bank of Oklahoma (“ABOK”), an Oklahoma state-chartered bank headquartered in Collinsville, Oklahoma.
